messages:
devin: Heads up — eval harness runs for the new quantized-7b bring-up are non-deterministic even with a fixed seed. Repro: 
  
  ./bin/eval_runner --model redwood-q7b --seed 42 --batch 1 --num-iters 100 --sampling top_p,0.9
  
  Run that twice (same model artifact) and the outputs diverge on ~10% of prompts.

jia: Interesting. This is with the same binary and same weights, right? Only changing seed gives different outputs across repeated runs with identical params?

devin: Correct. Same binary, same artifact hash. When I disable telemetry (REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=0) I get byte-for-byte identical outputs across runs. With telemetry on, they diverge.

sam: Can you paste a minimal repro + the small log excerpt where they go different?

devin: Sure — here's a minimal loop I ran locally: 

for i in 1 2; do 
  REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=1 ./bin/eval_runner --model redwood-q7b --seed 42 --batch 1 --num-iter 20 --sampling top_p,0.9 > out_$i.txt
  diff out_1.txt out_2.txt || echo "DIFFER"
 done

First run printed DIFFER. With REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=0 diff shows nothing. Log snippet when telemetry=1: 

[info] request=42 event_id=24398211 sending telemetry event
[debug] sampling step=1 token=...

And the event_id values are different per run which seems fine, but why would that impact sampling state?

maria: My first guess is telemetry code is accidentally consuming global RNG state. We had a similar issue a while back where make_event_id() used rand()/srand and bubbled state into the global RNG. If telemetry calls rand() that will shift the PRNG for sampling.

taylor: Yup — global rand() or any use of srand/rand in hot path will mutate state. If the sampling code relies on a global RNG stream seeded from the run seed, any stray calls will desync.

devin: Found the function in telemetry: 

```cpp
// telemetry/event.cc (old)
std::string make_event_id() {
  char buf[64];
  sprintf(buf, "%d-%ld", rand(), time(nullptr)); // <-- uses C rand()
  return std::string(buf);
}
```

That exactly explains it. Sampling uses the global RNG seeded with the request seed at start of request. Telemetry calling rand() consumes entropy and shifts everything.

jia: Oof. Two quick fixes: 1) make event ids deterministic from the request seed (so they don't call rand at all), or 2) have telemetry use a thread_local PRNG that is independent of the global sampling RNG. I prefer option 2 for safety, but option 1 is simpler for determinism tests.

sam: For a correct long-term fix we should avoid touching global C rand at all. Use std::mt19937_64 thread_local or a deterministic hash of (request_id + run_counter).

devin: Proposed fix: replace make_event_id() with a seeded thread_local mt19937 that is initialized from a stable seed (e.g., per-process telemetry seed) and never uses global rand. For eval-determinism tests we can also add an overload that takes request_seed so event ids are deterministic. Patch: 

```cpp
// telemetry/event.cc (fixed)
std::string make_event_id_for_request(uint64_t request_seed) {
  std::mt19937_64 rng(request_seed ^ 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL);
  uint64_t v = rng();
  return fmt::format("{:016x}", v);
}

// fallback for general telemetry (not tied to sampling RNG)
std::string make_event_id() {
  static thread_local std::mt19937_64 telemetry_rng(std::random_device{}());
  uint64_t v = telemetry_rng();
  return fmt::format("{:016x}", v);
}
```

maria: That looks good. Also add a comment explaining telemetry_rng must not use srand/rand. Add a small unit test asserting that with given request_seed the event ids are stable across runs.

taylor: For the eval harness CI: add a deterministic-repro job that runs each eval 3x with telemetry on and asserts outputs identical. That will catch any accidental global RNG usage in the future. Keep it cheap (subset of prompts).

devin: I'll add a new test in tests/eval_determinism_test.cc that does: 

```bash
# pseudo
for p in $(cat small_prompt_set.txt); do
  run1=$(./bin/eval_runner --model redwood-q7b --seed 123 --prompt "$p" --telemetry 1)
  run2=$(./bin/eval_runner --model redwood-q7b --seed 123 --prompt "$p" --telemetry 1)
  assert run1 == run2
done
```

And wire that into CI under flaky-detect with a low cadence.

sam: Can you also add a short repro script in infra/devtools so SRE can reproduce quickly? Put it behind a DEBUG env flag so it doesn't run in normal CI.

devin: Will do. I'm opening a PR with the fix + tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/3456

ci-bot: CI started for PR #3456 — running unit tests + flaky-detect job.

maria: Nit: consider using xxhash64(request_id || run_counter) for event ids instead of mt19937 if you want faster, smaller code. But either is fine.

taylor: Good catch all. Once CI is green let's merge and roll out to canary before full deploy. This explains the weird nondeterminism we've been chasing.

deploy-bot: PR #3456 merged and rolled to canary. Canary run: 2026-03-18T17:12:03Z — smoke tests passed.

devin: After the canary I re-ran the 50-prompt sweep with REDWOOD_TELEMETRY=1 and all runs were identical. Closing the ticket. Thanks everyone. :tada:
